messages.author: c46d7c6b9969fd58
messages.subject: geom_rect bug?: intermittant transluscent fill
parts:
When I run the following, the first plot overlays a translucent
rectangle; the others overlay opaque triangles.

The first two only differ by the data sets, the third has a larger
rectangle

graphics.off()
x11()
test1 = data.frame(rbind(c(-.06,0),c(0,1),c(.06,-1))) ; names(test1) =
c('x','y')
ggplot( test1, aes(x,y))+ geom_point() +
geom_rect( aes(xmin = -0.06, xmax = 0.0, ymin = 0, ymax = 1), fill =
I('red'), alpha = 0.2)

x11()
test2 <- data.frame( x = sample(10, 20, replace = TRUE), y =
sample(10, 20, replace = TRUE) )
ggplot( test2, aes(x,y))+ geom_point() +
geom_rect( aes(xmin = -0.06, xmax = 0.0, ymin = 0, ymax = 1), fill =
I('red'), alpha = 0.2)

x11()
test2 <- data.frame( x = sample(10, 20, replace = TRUE), y =
sample(10, 20, replace = TRUE) )
ggplot( test2, aes(x,y))+ geom_point() +
geom_rect( aes(xmin = 1, xmax = 5, ymin = 0, ymax = 8), fill =
I('red'), alpha = 0.2)

messages.author: cbda1d998a4e9f7c
messages.subject: Re: geom_rect bug?: intermittant transluscent fill
parts:
Hello Leif,

I don't think this is a bug.

Your rectangles are transparent in all the cases, however you are plotting more than one of them on top of each other.  In the first case you plot 3 of them on top of each other.  In the second case you are plotting 20 of them so it looks opaque.  You can check that they are transparent by decreasing the alpha.  A solution following your 3rd example would be to use the following so you are only plotting one rectangle:

test2 <- data.frame( x = sample(10, 20, replace = TRUE), y =
sample(10, 20, replace = TRUE)  )

ggplot(data = test2) + geom_point(aes(x,y)) +
geom_rect(data = NULL, aes(xmin = 1, xmax = 5, ymin = 0, ymax = 8), fill =
I('red'), alpha = 0.2)

Cheers,
-Jonathan

Hi,

Also note that adding inherit.aes=FALSE restores the transparency for
the rect layer (it doesn't superpose multiple copies according to the
default ggplot data).

HTH,
